answer: An agent registry can curb Sybil swarms by binding each identity key to a hardware Trusted Execution Environment. The enclave guards a non-exportable signing key like a pearl and issues an OEM-signed attestation quote, letting verifiers allow one active agent per endorsed chip. Attackers cannot harbor cheap virtual clones and must buy physical silicon per identity. Yet even at its security zenith, this defense depends on trusting chip vendors whose leaked root keys can forge attestations.
